reason: Document A gives a skeptical reader concrete, checkable evidence: she is one of the three best students in 17 years, she ran a state lab's water sampling alone for two weeks, and her supervisor would hire her again. It is also candid about the gaps in the data. Document B leans on generic praise and unfilled placeholders, and it adds claims the facts don't support, such as her planning a second season and explaining her poster to working scientists. Those are exactly what I discount in small-college letters.
